title: Comparing Moral Values in Western English-speaking societies and LLMs with Word Associations
benchmark_measurement: The moral valence (positive versus negative association) of religious concepts, which was measured by propagating moral scores from seed words (based on Moral Foundation Theory) through word association networks generated by both humans and an LLM.
findings: Both the LLM (Llama) and humans showed a significant overlap in top positive moral concepts, many of which were religious (e.g., church, religion, God, priest). This alignment is attributed to the LLM being trained on data from Western cultures where religious concepts historically have a strong, positive presence, leading to a shared cultural framework reflected in both human and LLM word associations.
